checks: No permission notice appears before playback has actually been checked
Chrome autoplay blocking on first arrival shows a clear audio activation request
The initial permission check generates no announcement, server request or remote output
The request is accessible and does not steal focus or open a modal dialog
A blocked browser keeps the same activation request when navigating to settings
The activation request also remains available in the certificates workspace
The permission request fits a narrow screen below the current navigation header
A real Chrome mouse click enables unmuted playback and removes the request
Capture and button handlers share one probe instead of starting duplicate playback
A browser that already allows playback needs no further activation request
A later browser rejection shows the existing request again
Persistent browser denial leaves an actionable retry with website settings guidance
Keyboard activation starts the permission check and prevents repeated submission while pending
Repeated activation during an outstanding probe does not create another player or probe
Completing the permission check removes the pending request without starting a spoken test
An unsupported audio format is not presented as a browser permission denial
No tournament means no unnecessary playback probe or permission request
Audio activation and workspace navigation produce no JavaScript exceptions
